title: Five-Dimensional Integrated Management Facilitates Successful Treatment of a Patient with Extreme Obesity and Sepsis Following Bariatric Surgery-A Case Report
content: Background: Extreme obesity is associated with difficult airway management, impaired respiratory mechanics, atelectasis, and difficult ventilator weaning. Postoperative infection and sepsis further increase management complexity. Case Report: A 27-year-old man with extreme obesity (BMI 60.97 kg/m²) developed Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection and sepsis after bariatric surgery. He was admitted to the ICU with respiratory failure and fluctuating consciousness. Multidisciplinary team (MDT) management was structured using an ABCDE-F framework centered on respiratory failure (F), together with analgesia and sedation (A), body position (B), circulation and perfusion (C), diet and nutrition (D), and early mobilization (E). This goal-directed approach supported successful extubation, infection control, and recovery. Conclusions: An MDT-based”five-dimensional integration”model may offer a practical framework for standardized, goal-directed management of critically ill patients with extreme obesity.
